subject.title: Rescue: add watchdog core service and cron engine

question: Should OpenClaw core accept an internal rescueWatchdog cron payload that can restart and doctor-repair managed gateway profiles once the branch is rebased and proven, or should this recovery loop stay external/operator-managed for now?
rationale: The implementation changes core cron protocol, persisted scheduler state, service-control behavior, and local repair command execution, so code review alone cannot decide the intended product/security boundary.

options.title: Sponsor core rescue after repairs
options.body: Keep this PR or a replacement open only after it preserves current cron contracts, adds store/protocol support, and shows real managed-gateway recovery proof.

options.title: Move recovery outside core
options.body: Close or redirect the branch if maintainers want watchdog recovery to remain an external script/plugin/operator pattern rather than a core cron payload.

options.title: Split daemon hardening only
options.body: Land only narrowly reviewed daemon/path hardening in a separate branch and defer rescueWatchdog semantics to a later product decision.

recommendation.title: Sponsor core rescue after repairs
recommendation.body: Keep this PR or a replacement open only after it preserves current cron contracts, adds store/protocol support, and shows real managed-gateway recovery proof.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc most recently merged the current cron/protocol/store surfaces that this branch must now integrate with.
